subject: Checkoutly: clarifying hosting vs. dedicated for low-latency checkout
messages:
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:06:00 -0700
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Chen <tim@checkoutly.com>, Hannah Price <hannah@checkoutly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Subject: Post-call: hosting vs dedicated — quick clarifying questions & next steps

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and two asks so we can size a clean recommendation.

Summary from our side:
- Checkout path is the most latency-sensitive feature; you said the user-visible latency spike happens on payment completion when we call the fraud scoring model.
- You indicated ~150 RPS steady, spiking to ~400 RPS for 10–30s during promotions, with p95 target ~70ms end-to-end for the scoring call.
- Compliance note: you prefer network isolation options but are open to a hosted pilot for initial validation.

Asks (feel free to reply inline):
1) Can you confirm the 95th percentile target you need for the model inference itself (you mentioned ~70ms; is that end-to-end or inference-only?)
2) For the traffic profile: can you share a 24-hr sample of RPS or a simple histogram (steady vs peak hours)?
3) Any restrictions on egress/KMS (do you need a customer-managed KMS for the pilot)?

Recommendation preview (high level):
- If inference-only p95 must be <80ms consistently at 400 RPS bursts: Dedicated capacity is the safer path (predictable latency and reserved kernels).
- If you can tolerate occasional 100–150ms tails and want fastest time-to-value: Hosted API pilot with burst reservations and a fallback to a slightly larger model variant may suffice.

Proposed next steps:
- You share the traffic sample and confirm p95 scope (inference-only vs end-to-end) — we’ll run a targeted latency-profile with both hosted and dedicated configs and share a side-by-side cost/latency comparison.
- We’ll prepare a 48-hour hosted stress test and a short Dedicated sizing proposal the week after.

Attaching a quick perf matrix we discussed (checkoutly-perf-matrix.xlsx).

Thanks — I can schedule the stress test next Tue/Wed if you’re available.

Best,
Sooj

Thanks for the recap, Sooj — helps a lot. Quick answers inline:

> 1) Can you confirm the 95th percentile target you need for the model inference itself (you mentioned ~70ms; is that end-to-end or inference-only?)
Inference-only target is what we care about — 70ms p95 inference. End-to-end currently runs ~200–300ms because of network + app logic; we want to avoid adding >50ms on top.

> 2) For the traffic profile: can you share a 24-hr sample of RPS or a simple histogram (steady vs peak hours)?
Attaching our 24-hr sample (see link below). Steady state: ~120–180 RPS; promo spikes to ~400 RPS for bursts 10–45s, maybe 4–6 times/day.

> 3) Any restrictions on egress/KMS (do you need a customer-managed KMS for the pilot?)
For the initial pilot we can use Redwood-managed KMS; if we go to Private later we’ll need customer-managed via AWS KMS.

One more thing — our security team will want a short writeup about fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity fails; they want to understand fallbacks to Hosted and any rate-limiting that could impact the checkout.

Tim

Subject: Re: Post-call: hosting vs dedicated — quick clarifying questions & next steps

Thanks — that clarifies a lot. Couple of notes and a concrete proposal below.

Notes:
- 70ms p95 inference-only at bursts to 400 RPS is a strong signal for Dedicated. The combination of reserved kernels, pinned colocated instances and conservative batching/caching will reduce tail variability.
- Hosted can meet lower steady loads easily; bursts are harder to guarantee without reserved capacity. We can do a hosted stress test but the risk is that ephemeral scheduling could add jitter in the window you care about.
- We support KMS integration later; for pilot using Redwood-managed KMS is fine.

Proposal (three-step path):
1) 48-hour Hosted stress test (this week) — purpose: reproduce the traffic pattern quickly and measure p95 tails across our multi-tenant runtime. Deliverable: latency/throughput report and list of tail causes.
2) Dedicated sizing proposal (48–72 hr turnaround) — configuration and committed capacity to meet 70ms p95 for the worst-case burst profile. Includes cost estimate and autoscale guardrails.
3) Mutual Action Plan (MAP) for a two-week Dedicated pilot if you choose that route; we’ll include a short SLA addendum and an emergency fallback policy description (how we fail safe to Hosted + throttling rules).

Next steps ask from Checkoutly:
- Confirm you want us to run the 48-hour Hosted stress test (we can start Tue 4 Aug)
- Share the traffic sample link (you sent a link — we have access) and any IP/CIDR allowlist we should use for test traffic

I’ve drafted a MAP and attached it (map-draft-Checkoutly.md). Also putting a short fallback description in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-checkoutly-pilot

If you’re OK I’ll loop Ben to approve a small pilot credit and reserved time on our infra calendar.

— Sooj
